title: Serre's criterion for normality
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Then $R$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] (every localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ at a prime is a normal domain) if and only if $R$ has properties $(R_1)$ and $(S_2)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal, line 43977), Serre's criterion for normality (EGA IV, Theorem 5.8.6), and its proof (via Lemma Tag 031R lemma-criterion-reduced, Tag 00PD lemma-characterize-dvr, Tag 0BHZ lemma-hart-serre-loc-thm, Tag 030C lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal)

proof.text: *Localizations inherit $(R_k)$ and $(S_k)$.* Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring with $(R_k)$ (resp. $(S_k)$) [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk], $\mathfrak p\subset R$ a prime and $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (1), (2), applied to $\lambda:R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ (a localization at $W=R\setminus\mathfrak p$), every prime $\mathfrak Q\subset A$ is $\mathfrak qA$ for the prime $\mathfrak q=\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)\subseteq\mathfrak p$ of $R$, and $A_{\mathfrak Q}\cong R_{\mathfrak q}$ as rings. A ring isomorphism of local rings preserves Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] and being regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]; so $\dim A_{\mathfrak Q}=\dim R_{\mathfrak q}$, and the conditions of $(R_k)$ (resp. $(S_k)$) for $A$ at $\mathfrak Q$ are those for $R$ at $\mathfrak q$. Hence $A$ has $(R_k)$ (resp. $(S_k)$). Moreover for a local ring $(A,\mathfrak m)$ the map $A\to A_{\mathfrak m}$ is an isomorphism, every element of $A\setminus\mathfrak m$ being a unit; so for a local ring the conditions at $\mathfrak m$ are conditions on $A$ itself: $(R_k)$ at $\mathfrak m$ says $A$ is regular if $\dim A\le k$, and $(S_k)$ at $\mathfrak m$ says $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge\min\{k,\dim A\}$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal, line 43977): the reduction to local rings in both directions ('it suffices to show that a local Noetherian ...')

proof.text:
*(1) $\Rightarrow$ (2), primes of height $\le1$.* Assume $R$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]: for every prime $\mathfrak p$ the ring $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a normal domain; it is Noetherian local (Step 0) of dimension $d=\dim A$, the height of $\mathfrak p$. If $d=0$: the zero ideal of the domain $A$ is prime, and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ is the only prime, so $\mathfrak m=0$ is generated by $0=\dim A$ elements and $A$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]; and $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge0=\min\{2,0\}$ trivially [def-weil-pbc-depth]. If $d=1$: $A$ is a Noetherian local normal domain of dimension $1$, hence a regular local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-dim-one-iff-normal]; and $\mathfrak m
e0$ (else $d=0$), so choose $0
e f\in\mathfrak m$; as $A$ is a domain, $f$ is a nonzerodivisor on $A$, and $A/fA
e0$ since $f$ is not a unit; so $(f)$ is a regular sequence in $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] and, as $\mathfrak mA
e A$, $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge1=\min\{2,1\}$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. (This is what the source takes from the criterion for reducedness and from the characterization of discrete valuation rings, for normal domains.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal, line 43977), first paragraph ('R has (R_0) and (S_1) by Lemma 031R ... The assertion if d = 1 follows from Lemma 00PD')

proof.text:
*(1) $\Rightarrow$ (2), depth when $d\ge2$.* Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] of dimension $d\ge2$ (possibly $d=\infty$ a priori). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kollar-local-dichotomy] (i) to $A$. Case (1) is impossible: an Artinian local ring has $\mathfrak m$ as its only prime [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime], so its dimension is $0$. Case (2) is impossible as $d
e1$. Suppose case (4): $\varphi:A	o A'$ finite, not an isomorphism, $A'
e0$, $\mathfrak m^n\ker\varphi=0$, $\mathfrak m^nA'\subseteq\varphi(A)$, no element of $A'$ with annihilator $\mathfrak m$. As $d\ge1$, $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak m$, so $\mathfrak m^n
e0$ in the domain $A$ and $\mathfrak m^n\ker\varphi=0$ forces $\ker\varphi=0$; identify $A\subseteq A'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated] applied to the finite $A$-module $A'$ there is $x\in\mathfrak m$ that is a nonzerodivisor on $A'$; $x
e0$ since $A'
e0$. Since $x^n\in\mathfrak m^n$, $x^ny\in A$ for every $y\in A'$. Let $K$ be the fraction field of $A$ and define $\iota:A'	o K$, $\iota(y)=(x^ny)/x^n$. It is additive, $\iota(1)=1$, and multiplicative because $x^n\cdot(x^ny)(x^nz)=x^{2n}\cdot(x^nyz)$ in $A'$, hence in $A$; it is injective because $x^ny=0$ forces $y=0$; and it restricts to the inclusion $A\subseteq K$. Every $y\in A'$ is integral over $A$ since $A'$ is a finite $A$-algebra [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], so $\iota(y)\in K$ is integral over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] and lies in $A$ because $A$ is integrally closed in $K$; by injectivity of $\iota$, $y\in A$. So $A'=A$ and $\varphi$ is an isomorphism, a contradiction. Hence case (3) holds: $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge2=\min\{2,d\}$ [def-weil-pbc-depth].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal, line 43977), second paragraph ('Apply Lemma 0BHZ to R ... Since m is not an associated prime of R' there exists x in m which is a nonzerodivisor on R'. Then R_x = R'_x ... Lemma 00GK ... R = R'')

proof.text: *Conclusion of (1) $\Rightarrow$ (2).* Let $R$ be a Noetherian normal ring and $\mathfrak p$ a prime, $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $d=\dim A$. If $d\le1$, $A$ is regular (Step 1): this is $(R_1)$. For every $\mathfrak p$, $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge\min\{2,d\}$ (Step 1 for $d\le1$, Step 2 for $d\ge2$): this is $(S_2)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal, line 43977)

proof.text: *(2) $\Rightarrow$ (1): the inductive claim.* Every Noetherian local ring has finite Krull dimension [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters]. We prove by strong induction on $d\ge0$ the claim $P(d)$: every Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring $(A,\mathfrak m)$ of dimension $d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] with $(R_1)$ and $(S_2)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk] is a normal domain. Given all $P(d)$: if $R$ has $(R_1)$ and $(S_2)$, then for every prime $\mathfrak p$ the ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian local of finite dimension with $(R_1)$ and $(S_2)$ (Step 0), hence a normal domain; so $R$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal, line 43977), third paragraph ('it suffices to show that if R is a reduced local Noetherian ring of dimension d satisfying (S_2) and (R_1) then R is a normal domain')

proof.text: *$A$ is reduced; the cases $d=0,1$.* Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be as in $P(d)$. Since $\min\{1,e\}\le\min\{2,e\}$ and height $0\le1$, $(S_2)$ implies $(S_1)$ and $(R_1)$ implies $(R_0)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk]; so $A$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-reduced]. If $d=0$: $\mathfrak m$ has height $0$, so by $(R_0)$ at $\mathfrak m$ (Step 0) $A$ is regular of dimension $0$ [def-weil-regular-scheme], i.e. $\mathfrak m$ is generated by $0$ elements, $\mathfrak m=0$ and $A$ is a field, which is a normal domain (it is its own fraction field) [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. If $d=1$: by $(R_1)$ at $\mathfrak m$ (Step 0) $A$ is a regular local ring of dimension $1$, hence a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-dim-one-iff-normal].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal, line 43977), third paragraph ('By Lemma 031R we conclude that R is reduced ... If d = 0, the result is clear. If d = 1, then the result follows from Lemma 00PD')

proof.text: *Case $d\ge2$: reduction to integral closedness in $Q(A)$.* Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be as in $P(d)$ with $d\ge2$, and assume $P(e)$ for all $e<d$. $A$ is reduced (Step 5) and Noetherian, so it has finitely many minimal primes [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes]. Let $S$ be the set of nonzerodivisors of $A$ and $Q(A)=S^{-1}A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; $A\to Q(A)$ is injective ($a/1=0$ means $sa=0$ for some $s\in S$, so $a=0$). By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-normal-iff-integrally-closed-total-fractions] ((2) $\Rightarrow$ (1)) it suffices to show that $A$ is integrally closed in $Q(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]: then $A$ is a normal ring, so $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and $A\cong A_{\mathfrak m}$ (Step 0). So let $x\in Q(A)$ be integral over $A$, with monic equation of degree $N\ge1$, and let $A'=A[x]\subseteq Q(A)$ be the $A$-subalgebra generated by $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] $A'$ is a finite $A$-module; indeed the monic equation shows that $1,x,\dots,x^{N-1}$ generate it as an $A$-module.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal, line 43977), fourth paragraph ('By Lemma 030C it suffices to show that R is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions Q(R). Pick x in Q(R) which is integral over R. Then R' = R[x] is a finite ring extension of R (Lemma 02JJ)')

proof.text:
*$A'$ and $A$ agree at every non-maximal prime.* Let $J=\{a\in A: aA'\subseteq A\}$, the annihilator of the $A$-module $A'/A$, an ideal. Let $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak m$ be a prime. A chain of primes in $A_{\mathfrak q}$ corresponds to a chain of primes of $A$ inside $\mathfrak q$ (Step 0), which extends by $\mathfrak m$; so $\dim A_{\mathfrak q}<d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is Noetherian local with $(R_1)$ and $(S_2)$ (Step 0 applied to $A$), so it is a normal domain by $P(\dim A_{\mathfrak q})$; let $K_{\mathfrak q}$ be its fraction field. For $s\in S$ the image $s/1\in A_{\mathfrak q}$ is nonzero (if $us=0$ with $u
otin\mathfrak q$ then $u=0\in\mathfrak q$, absurd), so it is invertible in $K_{\mathfrak q}$, and $\psi:Q(A)	o K_{\mathfrak q}$, $a/s\mapsto(a/1)(s/1)^{-1}$, is a well defined ring map extending $A	o A_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq K_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For $0\le k<N$, applying $\psi$ to a monic equation of $x^k$ over $A$ (powers of an integral element are integral, the integral elements forming a ring [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]) shows $\psi(x^k)$ is integral over $A_{\mathfrak q}$, hence $\psi(x^k)=a/t$ with $a\in A$, $t\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$, as $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is integrally closed in $K_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then $\psi(tx^k-a)=0$; writing $tx^k-a=b/s$ ($b\in A$, $s\in S$), $\psi(b/s)=0$ gives $b/1=0$ in $A_{\mathfrak q}$, i.e. $u_kb=0$ for some $u_k
otin\mathfrak q$, so $u_k(tx^k-a)=0$ in $Q(A)$ and $(u_kt)x^k=u_ka\in A$ with $u_kt
otin\mathfrak q$. The product $c$ of the elements $u_kt$ for $k=0,\dots,N-1$ lies outside $\mathfrak q$ and maps every generator $x^k$ of $A'$ into $A$, so $c\in J\setminus\mathfrak q$. Hence no prime $\mathfrak q
e\mathfrak m$ contains $J$. (This is Stacks' '$R_{\mathfrak p}=R'_{\mathfrak p}$ by induction'.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal, line 43977), fourth paragraph ('Because dim(R_p) < d for every nonmaximal prime p we have R_p = R'_p by induction. Hence the support of R'/R is {m}')

proof.text: *A power of $\mathfrak m$ kills $A'/A$.* If $J=A$ then $A'=A$ and $x\in A$. Otherwise $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and, by Step 7, $\mathfrak m$ is the only prime containing $J$; the radical of $J$ is the intersection of the primes containing $J$ [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], so $\sqrt J=\mathfrak m$. As $A$ is Noetherian, $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so $\mathfrak m^n\subseteq J$ for some $n\ge1$ [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power]: $\mathfrak m^nA'\subseteq A$. (This is the argument by which the source's lemma on supports gives the power of $\mathfrak m$.)

otin A$. By $(S_2)$ at $\mathfrak m$ (Step 0), $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge\min\{2,d\}=2$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]; as $\mathfrak mA
e A$ there is an $A$-regular sequence of length $\ge1$ in $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and its first element $f\in\mathfrak m$ is a nonzerodivisor of $A$, i.e. $f\in S$, a unit of $Q(A)$. Consider the inclusion $\varphi:A	o A'$: $A'
e0$, $A'$ is a finite $A$-module (Step 6), $\ker\varphi=0$, $\mathfrak m^nA'\subseteq A$ (Step 8), $\varphi$ is not an isomorphism ($x\in A'\setminus A$), and no $z\in A'$ has annihilator $\mathfrak m$: if $\mathfrak mz=0$ then $fz=0$ in $Q(A)$, so $z=0$, whose annihilator is $A
e\mathfrak m$. So $A$ has property (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-kollar-local-dichotomy] together with property (3) $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge2$, which (ii) of that lemma excludes. Hence $x\in A$, $A$ is integrally closed in $Q(A)$, and $A$ is a normal domain by Step 6. This proves $P(d)$ and, with Step 4, (2) $\Rightarrow$ (1).
